title_tag: 全球糖价上涨：粮食与能源之争—— 美国《纽约时报》外刊讲解第1202天
h1: 全球糖价上涨：粮食与能源之争
category: 美国《纽约时报》外刊讲解 第1202天
nav_hint: El Niño threatens global sugar supply

headline.en_html: El Niño Threatens Global Sugar Supply — A poor sugarcane crop in India, the world's second-largest producer, is hurting consumers and farmers — plus undermining the country's energy security goals.
headline.zh: 厄尔尼诺发威，全球糖供应告急——印度甘蔗歉收，正在让农民和消费者一起受伤，还把这个国家的能源安全目标，从底下一点点掏空。

notes.en: threaten (v.) means to be likely to cause harm or damage to something
notes.zh: 大祸临头但尚未落地的悬置感
notes.ctx: 糖还没断供，刀已经举起来了——作者不用 hurt 或 damage，因为它们表示“已经发生”，threaten 才是“即将发生”。
notes.ex1: The drought threatens the harvest of more than two million farmers. 这场干旱威胁着两百多万农民的收成。
notes.ex2: Warming seas threaten to push the fish stocks past the point of recovery. 海水变暖，可能会把鱼类资源推向无法恢复的临界点。

notes.en: supply (n.) means an amount of something that is available to be used
notes.ctx: 标题用 Global Sugar Supply，把一场天气事件直接接到了全世界的糖罐子上——五个词就交代了完整的因果链。
notes.ex1: Global oil supply remains tight despite record output in the United States. 尽管美国产量创纪录，全球石油供应依然吃紧。
notes.ex2: Fresh vegetables were in short supply after the floods. 洪水过后，新鲜蔬菜供应短缺。

notes.en: poor (adj.) means smaller in amount, or lower in quality, than is normal or expected
notes.ctx: a poor sugarcane crop 不是“一株穷甘蔗”，是“一场收成不好的甘蔗”；外刊经济类文章中 poor harvest 是固定高频搭配——典型熟词僻义。
notes.ex1: Poor harvests across the region have pushed bread prices to a record high. 整个地区歉收，把面包价格推到了历史新高。
notes.ex2: Investors were rattled by the company's poor results in the first quarter. 公司第一季度糟糕的业绩让投资者慌了神。

notes.en: undermine (v.) means to make something weaker at its most basic level, usually in a way that is not immediately noticeable
notes.ctx: 糖价一涨，印度能源安全目标的底座被一点点挖掉；作者不用 destroy——那是一下子炸掉，undermine 是你看不见的慢动作。
notes.ex1: Constant leaks undermined public confidence in the government's handling of the crisis. 不断出现的泄密，悄悄掏空了公众对政府处理这场危机的信任。
notes.ex2: Years of underfunding had undermined the foundations of the research system. 长年经费不足，已经把这套研究体系的根基掏空了。

paragraphs.en_html: Conflict. Climate change. A <mark class="voc">withering</mark> El Niño. All are <mark class="voc">conspiring</mark> to <mark class="voc">spoil</mark> the world's <mark class="voc">sweet tooth</mark>. Global sugar prices have <mark class="voc">soared</mark>, as a hot, dry summer scorched much of the sugar-producing parts of the world, <mark class="voc">nudging</mark> overall food prices upward. Nowhere is that felt as <mark class="voc">acutely</mark> as it is in India, the biggest sugar consumer in the world and the second-biggest producer. The worst <mark class="voc">monsoon</mark> in 11 years and fears of a poor sugarcane harvest have <mark class="voc">spiked</mark> prices amid the Hindu festival season, when gods and <mark class="voc">mortals</mark> alike are <mark class="voc">feted</mark> with sweets.
paragraphs.zh: 冲突。气候变化。一场正在让万物枯萎的厄尔尼诺。这三样东西像是商量好了似的，一起来毁掉全世界那份嗜甜的快乐。全球糖价一路飙升——一个又热又干的夏天，把世界上大片产糖区烤得焦头烂额，顺手把整体食品价格也往上顶了一顶。而这份痛，没有哪个地方感受得比印度更深切：它是全球最大的食糖消费国，也是第二大生产国。十一年来最糟糕的一场季风，加上对甘蔗歉收的恐惧，把糖价猛地戳了上去——偏偏这一切，就发生在印度教的节日季里；在这个时节，神明和凡人，都要用甜食供着。

notes.en: wither (v.) means if a plant withers, it becomes dry and dies
notes.ctx: withering 是现在分词作定语，修饰 El Niño，把一个自然现象写成了正在动手的反派；而这位反派的名字，叫“圣婴”。
notes.ex1: The crops withered in the fields for want of rain. 庄稼因为缺水，在田里活活枯死了。
notes.ex2: Their enthusiasm withered after the first few failures. 头几次失败之后，他们的热情就蔫了。

notes.en: conspire (v.) means to secretly plan with other people to do something harmful
notes.ctx: 战争、气候变化、厄尔尼诺三样互不相干的东西，被作者写成了一个犯罪团伙——用阴谋的动词写自然的巧合，这是外刊最爱的一手。
notes.ex1: High interest rates and weak demand conspired to sink the housing market. 高利率和需求疲软合谋，把楼市拖下了水。
notes.ex2: Everything seemed to conspire against her on the day of the interview. 面试那天，仿佛所有事情都在跟她作对。

notes.en: spoil (v.) means to ruin the quality or pleasure of something
notes.ctx: spoil the world's sweet tooth，把我们嗜甜的快乐给毁了——它和 sweet tooth 撞在一起，构成标题般的对仗。
notes.ex1: One bad apple can spoil the whole barrel. 一个烂苹果能坏掉一整桶。
notes.ex2: The rain spoiled what had been a perfect afternoon. 这场雨，糟蹋了一个原本完美的下午。

notes.en: sweet tooth (n.) means a strong liking for sweet food
notes.zh: 全世界那份嗜甜的快乐
notes.ctx: 作者不写 people's love of sugar，而写 the world's sweet tooth——把人类对甜食的依赖，写成了一颗具体的、会被伤害的牙。
notes.ex1: I have a sweet tooth, so I always keep a bar of dark chocolate in my bag. 我嗜甜，包里总揣着一块黑巧克力。
notes.ex2: She baked a cake to satisfy her son's sweet tooth. 她烤了个蛋糕，好满足儿子的甜食瘾。

notes.en: soar (v.) means to rise very quickly to a high level
notes.ctx: 三个“涨”里幅度最大的一个，Global sugar prices have soared；和 spike 的“啪一下”、nudge 的“轻轻推”构成递减阶梯。
notes.ex1: Housing prices have soared by more than 40 percent in five years. 房价五年里飙升了40% 以上。
notes.ex2: The rocket soared into the night sky. 火箭直窜夜空。

notes.en: nudge (v.) means to push someone or something gently, usually with your elbow
notes.zh: 顺带推高、温水煮青蛙式地推
notes.ctx: 糖价飙了，整体食品价格只被 nudge 了一下——因为糖在食品里占的比例小，天天买你感觉不到，月底看账单才发现贵了。
notes.ex1: The tax increase nudged inflation up by less than half a percentage point. 这次加税，把通胀轻轻往上顶了不到0.5 个百分点。
notes.ex2: She nudged her brother and pointed at the screen. 她用胳膊肘碰了碰弟弟，指了指屏幕。

notes.en: acutely (adv.) means in a sharp, intense way
notes.ctx: felt acutely 是痛感的强度；与前面 Nowhere 的倒装配合，构成“没有哪里比印度感受得更深切”。
notes.ex1: She was acutely aware that every eye in the room was on her. 她深切地意识到，屋里每一双眼睛都在看着她。
notes.ex2: The shortage is felt most acutely in rural areas. 这种短缺，在农村地区感受最深切。

notes.en: monsoon (n.) means the season of heavy rain in South Asia, or the wind that brings it
notes.ctx: the worst monsoon in 11 years——在印度，这不是气象新闻，是粮食新闻。
notes.ex1: Farmers across the country wait for the monsoon before planting. 全国农民都等季风到了才下种。
notes.ex2: A weak monsoon means a poor harvest for millions of small farmers. 季风一弱，就意味着数百万小农要歉收。

notes.en: spike (v.) means to rise suddenly and sharply
notes.ctx: 推高价格的不是“歉收”本身，而是 fears of a poor harvest——货还没少，人心先慌了；它和 soar 不同：soar 是持续飞高，spike 是“啪”的一下。
notes.ex1: Electricity prices spiked during the heat wave. 热浪期间，电价猛地蹿了上去。
notes.ex2: There was a sharp spike in unemployment after the factory closed. 工厂关停后，失业人数骤然飙升。

notes.en: mortal (n.) means a human being, especially one who will die; (adj.) means causing death, or too extreme to be defeated
notes.ctx: gods and mortals alike——神和凡人一视同仁，都被甜食供着；这个词为第十段那句“祷告”埋下了第一颗种子。
notes.ex1: In the old stories, gods and mortals shared the same table. 在古老的故事里，神明和凡人同桌共食。
notes.ex2: He spoke of things that mere mortals were not meant to know. 他讲的那些事，本不是凡人该知道的。

notes.en: fete (v.) means to honor or entertain someone with a celebration
notes.ctx: gods and mortals alike are feted with sweets——它是被动态，主语是神和凡人，动作是“被甜食招待”；外刊里这个词常用被动式。
notes.ex1: On her return she was feted as a national hero. 她归来时，被当作民族英雄一般盛情款待。
notes.ex2: Visitors are feted with tea and homemade cakes in every village. 每座村子里，来客都会用茶和自制糕点招待。

paragraphs.en_html: <mark class="voc">Making matters worse</mark>, high sugar prices are also <mark class="voc">complicating</mark> India's energy security goals. Sugarcane is a key crop for the country's biofuels push, all the more so as India seeks to curb oil imports while the waterways of the Middle East are <mark class="voc">choked</mark> by war. This year's El Niño has left many of the country's sugarcane fields <mark class="voc">parched</mark>, just a year after they were <mark class="voc">drenched</mark> by excess rains and <mark class="voc">devoured</mark> by pests.
paragraphs.zh: 更糟的是，高糖价还在把印度的能源安全目标搅成一团乱麻。甘蔗正是这个国家生物燃料计划的关键作物——这一点尤其要命，因为印度正想方设法压住石油进口，偏偏中东的航道又被战争掐住了。今年的厄尔尼诺，把印度大片甘蔗地晒得干裂；而就在一年前，这些地才刚被过多的雨水泡透、被害虫啃光。

notes.en: make matters worse means to make an already bad situation even worse
notes.ctx: 前面讲的是厨房里的糖，这一插入语一出来，场子立刻扩到了加油站和国家战略。
notes.ex1: It was raining, and, to make matters worse, the car broke down. 天在下雨，更糟的是，车还抛了锚。
notes.ex2: The crops failed. What's worse, the price of seed had doubled. 庄稼歉收了。更糟的是，种子价格翻了一倍。

notes.en: complicate (v.) means to make a problem or situation more difficult to deal with
notes.ctx: 作者不说 hurt、不说 damage、不说 threaten——他选 complicate：能源安全这事本来就难，现在又多了一团乱麻；麻烦不是被炸掉的，是被搅浑的。
notes.ex1: The strike further complicated an already difficult negotiation. 罢工让本就艰难的谈判更添了一团乱麻。
notes.ex2: A shortage of drivers has complicated the delivery of the supplies. 司机短缺，给物资运送添了乱。

notes.en: choke (v.) means to make it difficult for someone to breathe; to block something so nothing can pass through
notes.ctx: the waterways of the Middle East are choked by war——一只手掐在航道上，船过不去。
notes.ex1: The narrow streets were choked with traffic all day. 那些窄街，一整天都堵得水泄不通。
notes.ex2: His voice was choked with emotion as he thanked the crowd. 他向人群道谢时，声音因激动而哽咽。

notes.en: parched (adj.) means very dry, especially because of hot weather
notes.ctx: left the fields parched——它与下文的 drenched 构成一对：去年泡透，今年烤干。
notes.ex1: After three months without rain, the fields were parched and cracked. 三个月没下雨，田地干裂，裂开一道道缝。
notes.ex2: He drank three glasses of water to soothe his parched throat. 他灌了三杯水，好缓解冒烟的嗓子。

notes.en: drench (v.) means to make someone or something completely wet
notes.ctx: drenched by excess rains——老天爷不给中间值：去年泡透，今年烤干。
notes.ex1: We were drenched to the skin before we reached the car. 还没走到车边，我们就被浇了个透。
notes.ex2: The sudden storm drenched the fields in less than an hour. 那场急风暴雨，不到一小时就把田地泡透了。

notes.en: devour (v.) means to eat something quickly and hungrily, like an animal
notes.ctx: devoured by pests——虫子用的是野兽吞食的动词；三个动词连起来就是印度农民这两年：drenched 泡透→devoured 啃光→parched 烤干。
notes.ex1: The locusts devoured the crop in a single night. 蝗虫一夜之间把庄稼啃了个精光。
notes.ex2: She devoured the novel in two days. 她两天就把那本小说啃完了。

paragraphs.en_html: Protests have <mark class="voc">broken out</mark> over rising prices. The government has warned sugar traders against <mark class="voc">hoarding</mark>. And a country that usually exports sugar has <mark class="voc">taken the extraordinary step of</mark> opening the doors to imports this year, further raising global sugar prices. "This crop is gone," Morarji Patil, a 30-year-old farmer, said as he stood beside his cane field one sweaty September morning in the Marathwada region of western India. Like other farmers here, Mr. Patil was already <mark class="voc">crushed</mark> by debt and high fertilizer prices before the <mark class="voc">blistering</mark> heat and <mark class="voc">scant</mark> rains. His cane <mark class="voc">stalks</mark> were thin and short, <mark class="voc">stunted</mark> by a lack of water this summer when they needed it most. Mr. Patil expected his <mark class="voc">yields</mark> to be 70 percent lower than normal.
paragraphs.zh: 抗议因涨价而爆发了。政府已经警告糖商不许囤积。而一个平时出口糖的国家，今年破天荒地迈出一步——向进口打开了大门，这反过来又把全球糖价往上推了一把。“这批庄稼完了。”三十岁的农民莫拉尔吉·帕蒂尔说。那是一个出汗的九月早晨，他站在印度西部马拉特瓦达地区自家的甘蔗地边。跟这里其他农民一样，在酷热和少雨到来之前，他就已经被债务和高昂的化肥价格压垮了。他的甘蔗秆又细又矮——在最需要水的那个夏天，水没来。帕蒂尔预计，今年的收成会比正常年份低七成。

notes.en: break out means if something such as war, fire or fighting breaks out, it starts suddenly
notes.ctx: Protests have broken out over rising prices——over 在这里不是“在……上面”，是“因为”。
notes.ex1: Protests broke out in three cities after the fuel price rose. 油价上涨后，三座城市爆发了抗议。
notes.ex2: A fire broke out in the kitchen late at night. 深夜，厨房起了火。

notes.en: hoard (v.) means to collect and store large amounts of something, often in secret
notes.ctx: 老百姓一慌，糖商就囤，一囤就更贵，更贵就更慌，这是个死循环，所以政府直接下场限库存。
notes.ex1: Shoppers hoarded toilet paper as soon as the news broke. 消息一出，顾客就抢着囤卫生纸。
notes.ex2: They hoarded supplies, hoping to sell them at a higher price. 他们把货囤起来，指望着能卖个高价。

notes.en: take the step of doing something means to do something important that you have been considering
notes.ctx: 不说 has decided to import，因为这一步不是随便迈的。
notes.ex1: The government took the extraordinary step of closing the airports. 政府破天荒地迈出了一步：关闭机场。
notes.ex2: She finally took the step of starting her own business. 她终于迈出了那一步——自己创业。

notes.en: crush (v.) means to press something so hard that it breaks or is damaged
notes.zh: 在旱灾到来之前，就已经被压垮了
notes.ctx: was already crushed by debt ... before the blistering heat——天灾不是起因，天灾是最后一击。
notes.ex1: Many small farmers are crushed by debt before the first crop is sold. 许多小农在头一茬庄稼卖出之前，就已被债务压垮。
notes.ex2: The news crushed her hopes of going to university. 这个消息，碾碎了她上大学的希望。

notes.en: blistering (adj.) means extremely hot, or done with great speed, force or anger
notes.ctx: the blistering heat——外刊里 blistering 常形容热、快、狠三层意思，如 a blistering attack 一顿猛批。
notes.ex1: Workers laboured in blistering heat to repair the road. 工人们在酷热中修路。
notes.ex2: The minister came under blistering criticism from both sides. 部长受到来自双方的猛烈批评。

notes.en: scant (adj.) means not enough; very small in amount
notes.ctx: scant rains——与前面的 crushed by debt 一起，构成债务→化肥贵→酷热→少雨，一件件往上摞。
notes.ex1: The team paid scant attention to the warnings. 那支队伍几乎没把警告当回事。
notes.ex2: There is scant evidence that the policy has worked. 几乎没有证据表明这项政策起了作用。

notes.en: stalk (n.) means the main stem of a plant; (v.) means to follow someone secretly and persistently
notes.ctx: His cane stalks were thin and short——一年生的秆子又细又矮，说明它在最需要水的夏天，没喝到水。
notes.ex1: He pulled a stalk of sugarcane from the field to show us. 他从地里拔出一根甘蔗秆给我们看。
notes.ex2: In the old photograph, the corn stalks were taller than the boy. 那张老照片里，玉米秆比那孩子还高。

notes.en: stunt (v.) means to prevent something from growing to its full size; (n.) a dangerous action done for entertainment
notes.ctx: stunted by a lack of water——过去分词短语作原因状语，解释甘蔗为什么又细又矮。
notes.ex1: Her growth was stunted by years of poor nutrition. 长年营养不良，阻碍了她的发育。
notes.ex2: The company staged a publicity stunt to launch the new phone. 公司为发布新手机，搞了一次博眼球的噱头活动。

notes.en: yield (n.) means the amount of food produced on an area of land; (v.) means to produce or to give way
notes.ctx: expected his yields to be 70 percent lower than normal——三户农民连成一条递减线：七成→一半→四分之一。
notes.ex1: Crop yields fell by nearly a third after the drought. 干旱之后，粮食产量下降了近三分之一。
notes.ex2: The new seeds give a higher yield per acre. 新种子让每亩产量更高了。

paragraphs.en_html: India represents an <mark class="voc">object lesson</mark> on the <mark class="voc">far-reaching</mark> effects of conflict and extreme weather on a nation's economy. Food prices are rising month by month. Key crops <mark class="voc">remain at risk</mark> as <mark class="voc">the long tail</mark> of El Niño drags out through next year, heightening the <mark class="voc">likelihood</mark> of extreme drought and flood. <mark class="voc">On top of that</mark>, India is extremely <mark class="voc">vulnerable</mark> to global oil supply shocks. It imports the vast majority of its crude oil. It's not just India. <mark class="voc">Extraordinary</mark> heat and drought this year have <mark class="voc">hit</mark> sugarcane in Brazil, the world's biggest sugar producer, and <mark class="voc">sugar beets</mark> in Europe. Global sugar prices are nearly 15 percent higher than they were a year ago.
paragraphs.zh: 印度就是一件摆在眼前的活教材——它演示了冲突和极端天气，能对一个国家的经济产生多深远的影响。食品价格一个月一个月地往上走。关键作物依然岌岌可危，因为厄尔尼诺那条长尾巴还要一路拖到明年，把极端干旱和洪水发生的可能性又抬高了。雪上加霜的是，印度在全球石油供应冲击面前，脆弱得不堪一击——它绝大部分的原油都靠进口。而且，倒霉的不止印度一个。今年破纪录的高温和干旱，同时打击了巴西的甘蔗和欧洲的甜菜——前者是全球最大的产糖国。全球糖价，已经比一年前高出将近15%。

notes.en: an object lesson is a clear, practical example of how something should or should not be done
notes.ctx: 印度用自己的经济，给全世界演示了一遍战争加极端天气能把一个国家搞成什么样；注意：它绝不是“物体课”，这是本段最大的陷阱。
notes.ex1: The collapse of the bank was an object lesson in what happens when regulation is weak. 那家银行的倒闭，是监管松懈会酿成什么后果的活教材。
notes.ex2: Every failed project should be treated as an object lesson. 每一个失败的项目，都该被当作摆在眼前的教材。

notes.en: far-reaching (adj.) means having a wide influence or effect
notes.ctx: far-reaching effects of conflict and extreme weather——一条因果链从太平洋一直伸到印度人的餐桌。
notes.ex1: The decision had far-reaching consequences for the whole industry. 这个决定对整个行业产生了深远影响。
notes.ex2: They announced far-reaching reforms of the tax system. 他们宣布了对税制影响深远的改革。

notes.en: remain at risk means to continue to be in a situation where something bad could happen
notes.ctx: Key crops remain at risk——不是“现在危险”，是“危险的状态一直没解除”。
notes.ex1: Hundreds of homes remain at risk from the rising water. 数百户人家仍处在上涨的洪水威胁之下。
notes.ex2: The harvest remains at risk until the rains arrive. 雨不来，收成就一直悬着。

notes.en: the long tail means the effect of something that continues long after the main event is over
notes.zh: 厄尔尼诺拖在后面的那条尾巴
notes.ctx: the long tail of El Niño drags out through next year——它今年闹完，明年还拖着你。
notes.ex1: Doctors warn of the long tail of the disease, which can last for years. 医生警告这种病有很长的尾巴，可能持续数年。
notes.ex2: Even after the war ended, its long tail was felt for a generation. 战争结束了，它的长尾效应还影响了一代人。

notes.en: likelihood (n.) means the chance that something will happen
notes.ctx: heightening the likelihood of extreme drought and flood——尾巴一拖，概率就上去了。
notes.ex1: There is a strong likelihood of rain later this week. 本周晚些时候极有可能下雨。
notes.ex2: The new treatment reduces the likelihood of complications. 新疗法降低了出现并发症的可能性。

notes.en: on top of that means in addition to what has been said, especially when it is bad
notes.ctx: On top of that, India is vulnerable to oil shocks——已经一堆事了，又往上摞了一件。
notes.ex1: It rained for a week and, on top of that, the hotel lost our booking. 雨下了一周，更糟的是，酒店还把我们的预订弄丢了。
notes.ex2: He lost his job and, to top it all off, his car broke down. 他丢了工作，雪上加霜的是，车还坏了。

notes.en: vulnerable (adj.) means able to be easily hurt or harmed, especially because you have no protection
notes.ctx: vulnerable to global oil supply shocks——一个国家的两个命门，吃的和烧的，同时被掐住了。
notes.ex1: Older people are especially vulnerable to extreme heat. 老年人尤其容易受到极端高温的伤害。
notes.ex2: The country remains highly vulnerable to oil supply shocks. 这个国家在石油供应冲击面前，依然极其脆弱。

notes.en: extraordinary (adj.) means very unusual or surprising
notes.ctx: 一个常年出口糖的国家，如今开门进口——这个动作本身就是 extraordinary。
notes.ex1: The hospital took extraordinary measures to save the patient. 医院采取了非常规手段去抢救那个病人。
notes.ex2: It was an extraordinary achievement for a first novel. 对一部处女作来说，那是了不起的成就。

notes.en: hit (v.) means to affect someone or something very badly
notes.ctx: have hit sugarcane in Brazil and sugar beets in Europe——灾害类外刊的万能动词：不说 damage，不说 affect，像一拳打过来，一拳打在两处。
notes.ex1: The drought hit the harvest across three provinces. 干旱打击了三个省的收成。
notes.ex2: The tourism industry was hit hard by the pandemic. 旅游业受到疫情的重创。

notes.en: sugar beet means a plant with a large white root from which sugar is made
notes.ctx: 今年两条腿一起挨打——巴西的甘蔗和欧洲的甜菜同时受灾。
notes.ex1: Much of Europe's sugar comes from sugar beet rather than cane. 欧洲的糖大部分来自甜菜，而不是甘蔗。
notes.ex2: The sugar beet crop suffered badly in the dry summer. 那个干旱的夏天里，甜菜收成糟糕透顶。

paragraphs.en_html: In India, sugar has long <mark class="voc">enjoyed</mark> state support. Most recently, the industry <mark class="voc">profited from</mark> a government <mark class="voc">directive</mark> that made 20-percent <mark class="voc">ethanol</mark> <mark class="voc">blends</mark> the standard fuel at Indian gas stations. The government said its biofuels push reduced oil demand and climate pollution, while also saving the country's <mark class="voc">precious</mark> <mark class="voc">foreign exchange</mark>. It called ethanol blends "a key <mark class="voc">pillar</mark> of India's energy transition." It offered sugar <mark class="voc">refineries</mark> an additional source of revenue. It also <mark class="voc">infuriated</mark> Indian drivers.
paragraphs.zh: 在印度，糖长期以来都享受着国家的扶持。最近，这个行业从一项政府指令里赚到了钱——这项指令把含20% 乙醇的混合燃油，定为印度加油站的标准燃油。政府说，它推的这套生物燃料，既压低了石油需求和气候污染，又省下了国家宝贵的外汇。它把这种乙醇燃油称作“印度能源转型的一根关键支柱”。它给糖厂送去了一笔额外收入。它同时也把印度司机气炸了。

notes.en: enjoy (v.) means to have and be able to use something good or useful
notes.ctx: sugar has long enjoyed state support——糖不是普通商品，它被政策抱在怀里。
notes.ex1: The industry has long enjoyed protection from the state. 这个行业长期以来享受着国家的保护。
notes.ex2: He enjoys a reputation as one of the finest chefs in the city. 他享有这座城市最好厨师之一的名声。

notes.en: profit from something means to get an advantage or money from it
notes.ctx: 作者不用 benefited from，因为 profit 把“赚钱”两个字写在脸上了。
notes.ex1: The company profited handsomely from the rise in demand. 公司从需求上涨中大赚了一笔。
notes.ex2: He profited from information that other investors did not have. 他靠别的投资者没有的信息赚了钱。

notes.en: directive (n.) means an official order or instruction
notes.zh: 一道让糖厂赚钱的政令
notes.ctx: 直接把20% 乙醇汽油定成全国加油站的标配。
notes.ex1: The ministry issued a directive ordering all schools to close. 部里下达指令，要求所有学校关闭。
notes.ex2: Under the new directive, every station must sell the blended fuel. 按新指令，每个加油站都必须出售这种混合燃油。

notes.en: ethanol (n.) means a type of alcohol that can be used as a fuel, made from plants such as sugarcane or corn
notes.zh: 掺进汽油里的那种酒精
notes.ctx: 20-percent ethanol blends——印度把它叫 E20，2026 年4 月起成为全国加油站标配。
notes.ex1: Brazil has used ethanol as a vehicle fuel for decades. 巴西把乙醇当车用燃料用了几十年。
notes.ex2: The government ordered more ethanol to be blended into petrol. 政府下令在汽油中掺入更多乙醇。

notes.en: blend (n.) means a mixture of different things; (v.) to mix things together
notes.ctx: ethanol blends——司机加的不再是纯汽油，而是一份掺出来的东西。
notes.ex1: The new fuel is a blend of petrol and ethanol. 这种新燃料是汽油和乙醇的混合物。
notes.ex2: The city is a blend of old and new. 这座城市是新旧交融的产物。

notes.en: precious (adj.) means rare and valuable, and therefore worth protecting
notes.ctx: saving the country's precious foreign exchange——对一个高度依赖进口的国家，外汇是命根子，所以作者给它加了“珍贵”两个字。
notes.ex1: Every drop of water became precious during the drought. 干旱期间，每一滴水都变得金贵起来。
notes.ex2: The country spends precious foreign exchange importing fuel. 这个国家花掉宝贵的外汇去进口燃料。

notes.en: foreign exchange means the system of buying and selling foreign money; the money a country holds in other currencies
notes.ctx: 印度每少进口一桶油，就少花一笔美元；对一个高度依赖进口的国家，外汇是命根子。
notes.ex1: Every barrel it no longer imports saves precious foreign exchange. 每少进口一桶油，就省下一笔宝贵的外汇。
notes.ex2: The central bank stepped in to defend the currency with its foreign reserves. 央行出手，动用外汇储备保卫本币。

notes.en: pillar (n.) means a strong column that supports a building; something important that supports a system
notes.ctx: 不是“一个办法”，是“支柱”：抽了它就塌。
notes.ex1: Farming remains a pillar of the local economy. 农业仍是当地经济的支柱。
notes.ex2: She was a pillar of strength to her family throughout the crisis. 整场危机中，她都是全家的顶梁柱。

notes.en: refinery (n.) means a factory where a substance such as oil or sugar is made pure
notes.ctx: 第5 段结尾那句 It offered sugar refineries an additional source of revenue，说的就是它们。
notes.ex1: The sugar refinery runs day and night during the harvest. 收成季里，糖厂日夜不停地运转。
notes.ex2: Oil refineries along the coast were forced to shut down. 沿海的那些炼油厂被迫关停。

notes.en: infuriate (v.) means to make someone extremely angry
notes.ctx: 与前一句 It offered sugar refineries... 构成并列的两个短句：一手给糖，一手给巴掌；作者连一个转折词都没用。
notes.ex1: The new charges infuriated commuters across the city. 新的收费把全城的通勤者气炸了。
notes.ex2: She was infuriated by his refusal to answer the question. 他拒绝回答那个问题，把她气坏了。

paragraphs.en_html: Aditya Kare, 21, was <mark class="voc">refueling</mark> his 2018 Hero motorcycle at a gas station in the nearby city of Latur. He said the ethanol blend had reduced his average <mark class="voc">mileage</mark> from 60 kilometers per liter to around 45, and he was having a hard time <mark class="voc">making do with</mark> the 100 rupees, a little more than $1, that his parents gave him for his <mark class="voc">commute</mark> to college. "At home, we are planning to get an electric bike," he said.
paragraphs.zh: 21 岁的阿迪蒂亚·卡雷，正在附近的拉图尔市一座加油站，给他那辆2018 款的Hero 摩托车加油。他说，乙醇混合燃油把他的平均油耗，从每升60 公里压到了45 公里左右——父母给他上学通勤的那100 卢比（也就比一美元多一点），他越来越难凑合着撑过去了。“我们家正打算买一辆电动车，”他说。

notes.en: refuel (v.) means to put more fuel into a vehicle
notes.ctx: was refueling his 2018 Hero motorcycle——全篇唯一一个动态画面：一个年轻人，站在加油站。
notes.ex1: He pulled into the station to refuel before the long drive. 他把车开进加油站，好在长途驾驶前加满油。
notes.ex2: The plane landed to refuel and took off an hour later. 飞机降落加油，一小时后重新起飞。

notes.en: mileage (n.) means the number of miles a vehicle can travel using a particular amount of fuel
notes.ctx: from 60 kilometers per liter to around 45——换算过来是百公里1.67 升变成了2.22 升，多烧三分之一。
notes.ex1: The car's mileage fell after they switched to the new fuel. 换成新燃料后，这辆车的油耗明显变差了。
notes.ex2: He checked the mileage before deciding whether to buy it. 他先看了油耗，再决定买不买。

notes.en: make do with something means to manage with what you have, even though it is not really enough
notes.ctx: 那100 卢比约合1 美元多，也就是7 块多人民币，是他一天上学的钱。
notes.ex1: We had no bread, so we had to make do with rice. 没有面包了，我们只能拿米饭凑合。
notes.ex2: She made do with what she had and never complained. 她手头有什么就用什么，从不抱怨。

notes.en: commute (n.) means the journey to work or school and back every day
notes.ctx: 父母给他那100 卢比，是让他去上学的。
notes.ex1: His commute to college takes almost an hour each way. 他上学单程就要将近一小时。
notes.ex2: More people are choosing to commute by bike in the city. 城里越来越多人选择骑车通勤。

paragraphs.en_html: Sugarcane <mark class="voc">comes with</mark> a high cost. It is a <mark class="voc">thirsty</mark> crop, and its demand, for both food and fuel, is forcing many farmers to <mark class="voc">drill</mark> deeper for water and <mark class="voc">drain</mark> local <mark class="voc">aquifers</mark>. Mr. Patil's well goes down 800 feet. This year, even at that depth, there is no water. A dam on the Manjara River has become a dry <mark class="voc">ditch</mark>. Ponds are <mark class="voc">bare</mark>. "This environment is not good for sugarcane," said Ganesh Gomare, a farmer. "But the economy of Marathwada is dependent on sugarcane."
paragraphs.zh: 甘蔗，是带着高昂代价来的。它是一种很“渴”的作物，而它作为食物与燃料的双重需求，正逼着许多农民往更深处打井，把当地的地下含水层抽干。帕蒂尔家的井，往下打了800 英尺——可今年，打到了那个深度，依然没有水。曼贾拉河上的那座水坝，如今成了一条干沟。池塘，空空如也。“这方水土，不适合种甘蔗，”农民加内什·戈马雷说。“可马拉特瓦达的经济，就靠甘蔗撑着。”

notes.en: come with something means to include something as a part or feature, or to have it as a necessary result
notes.zh: 代价是跟着甘蔗一起长出来的
notes.ctx: 不说 has a high cost，因为 comes with 的意思是：你种它，这份代价就和它一起长出来了，掰不开。
notes.ex1: Every choice comes with a cost. 每一个选择，都带着代价。
notes.ex2: The apartment comes with a small garage. 这套公寓带一个小车库。

notes.en: thirsty (adj.) means needing to drink; used of plants, needing a lot of water
notes.ctx: a thirsty crop——生产一公斤蔗糖，从种到炼全程要耗掉一千多升水。
notes.ex1: Sugarcane is a thirsty crop, and the wells are running dry. 甘蔗是喝水大户，而井正在见底。
notes.ex2: After two hours in the sun, the workers were thirsty and tired. 在太阳下干了两个小时，工人们又渴又累。

notes.en: drill (v.) means to make a hole in the ground using a special machine, in order to find water or oil
notes.ctx: 不是农民想打井，是需求在逼他们打。
notes.ex1: Farmers are drilling deeper each year to reach the falling water table. 农民们一年比一年钻得深，去够那越来越低的水位。
notes.ex2: They drilled for oil for three years and found nothing. 他们钻了三年石油，一无所获。

notes.en: drain (v.) means to make the water in something flow away, so that it becomes empty
notes.ctx: 地下那块储存水的“海绵”，正在被抽空。
notes.ex1: Years of overuse have drained the aquifer beneath the plain. 长年超采，把平原下面的含水层抽干了。
notes.ex2: The project drained the swamp and turned it into farmland. 这项工程抽干了沼泽，把它变成了农田。

notes.en: aquifer (n.) means a layer of rock or soil under the ground that holds water
notes.zh: 农民往上钻的那块海绵
notes.ctx: 井打得越深，这块海绵就干得越快。
notes.ex1: The local aquifer has fallen by several metres in ten years. 当地含水层十年间下降了好几米。
notes.ex2: Once an aquifer is drained, it may take centuries to refill. 含水层一旦被抽干，可能要几个世纪才能重新蓄满。

notes.en: ditch (n.) means a narrow channel dug in the ground, used for water or drainage
notes.zh: 大坝自己变成了一条干沟
notes.ctx: 本该把水拦住的东西，现在自己成了漏水的沟。
notes.ex1: The stream behind the village is little more than a ditch now. 村后那条小溪，如今几乎只剩一条沟了。
notes.ex2: Workers dug a ditch to carry the water to the fields. 工人们挖了一条沟，把水引到田里。

notes.en: bare (adj.) means empty, with nothing in it or covering it
notes.ctx: Ponds are bare——三个词，一个句号；作者写完就闭了嘴，这句不要去解释，停两秒。
notes.ex1: The shelves were bare by the end of the day. 一天下来，货架空了。
notes.ex2: The trees stood bare against the winter sky. 树木光秃秃的，立在冬天的天空下。

paragraphs.en_html: Sugar is <mark class="voc">tempting</mark>. It enjoys relatively high profits. So Mr. Gomare, 38, <mark class="voc">devoted</mark> more of his land to sugarcane this year. It <mark class="voc">backfired</mark>. He expects his yields to be half of normal.
paragraphs.zh: 糖是诱人的。它利润相对高。所以38 岁的戈马雷先生今年把更多的地，押给了甘蔗。适得其反。他预计，收成只有正常年份的一半。

notes.en: tempting (adj.) means making you want to have or do it, even though you know you probably should not
notes.zh: 明知有风险，还是忍不住
notes.ctx: 马拉特瓦达的水本就不够，可甘蔗利润高，糖厂就在旁边。
notes.ex1: The offer was tempting, but she knew the risks were too great. 那份报价很诱人，但她知道风险太大了。
notes.ex2: The cake looked tempting, and he had not eaten since morning. 那块蛋糕看着太勾人，而他一早到现在还没吃东西。

notes.en: devote A to B means to give a large part of your time, effort or resources to one particular thing
notes.ctx: 他不是被骗去种的，他是主动押的注。
notes.ex1: He devoted more of his land to the crop that promised the highest price. 他把更多的地，押在了那个承诺价最高的作物上。
notes.ex2: She devoted herself to teaching for more than thirty years. 她献身教育三十多年。

notes.en: backfire (v.) means if a plan or action backfires, it has the opposite result to the one you intended
notes.ctx: 两句话铺垫押注，两个字把它全部炸回来——这是英文写作里最狠的一招：长铺短收。
notes.ex1: The plan to save money backfired and cost them twice as much. 省钱的反倒花掉了两倍的钱。
notes.ex2: His joke backfired on him when nobody laughed. 没人笑，他那个笑话反噬到了自己身上。

paragraphs.en_html: Nearby, Dagdu Venkat Rao Padile, 66, <mark class="voc">uprooted</mark> a stalk of sugarcane from his field. The plant was <mark class="voc">emaciated</mark>. Its sugar content would be <mark class="voc">paltry</mark>. "It will cost me more to cut it than what I'll get for it," Mr. Padile said. His yields would be one-fourth of normal. The rains were so poor that he had left most of his land <mark class="voc">fallow</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 不远处，66 岁的达格杜·文卡特·拉奥·帕迪尔，从自家地里连根拔起了一根甘蔗。这株植物瘦得脱了形。它的含糖量，会少得可怜。“割它花的钱，比卖它能挣的还多，”帕迪尔说。他估摸着，今年的收成只有正常年份的四分之一。雨水少成那样，他干脆把大部分地都撂荒了。

notes.en: uproot (v.) means to pull a plant out of the ground, including its roots
notes.ctx: 割，是为了收；拔，是为了看：他想知道这根甘蔗到底长成了什么样。
notes.ex1: He uprooted a cane and held it up for us to see how thin it was. 他拔出一根甘蔗举起来，让我们看它有多细。
notes.ex2: Thousands of families were uprooted by the war. 战争让数千家庭背井离乡。

notes.en: emaciated (adj.) means extremely thin and weak, especially because of illness or lack of food
notes.ctx: 作者把一个本来形容人和动物的词用在一根植物上，一个词就把甘蔗写成了营养不良的孩子，而它饿，是因为最需要水的那个夏天，水没来。
notes.ex1: The rescuers found children too emaciated to stand. 救援人员发现的那些孩子，瘦得站都站不起来。
notes.ex2: After months without rain, the plants looked emaciated. 几个月没下雨，那些植物看上去都饿瘦了。

notes.en: paltry (adj.) means very small in amount, and of little or no value
notes.ctx: 一根甘蔗的全部价值就在它的糖上，而今年糖也少得可怜。
notes.ex1: They were offered a paltry sum for a year's work. 干了一年，他们只拿到一笔少得可怜的钱。
notes.ex2: The raise was so paltry that nobody bothered to thank anyone. 那点加薪少得可怜，没人愿意为它道谢。

notes.en: fallow (adj.) means if land is left fallow, it is not planted with crops for a season, to let the soil recover
notes.ctx: 他不是想让地歇，是种不起；一个农民把地空着，是他这辈子最难受的事。
notes.ex1: With no water in the wells, he left most of his land fallow. 井里没水，他只好把大部分地撂荒。
notes.ex2: Farmers let the fields lie fallow every third year. 农民们每三年让地休耕一次。

paragraphs.en_html: Tanisha Gaikwad had <mark class="voc">all but</mark> cut sugar from her diet. But she <mark class="voc">joined the line</mark> at the sweet shop for a small box of laddoos to offer at the <mark class="voc">altar</mark> for Mahalaxmi, a goddess of wealth and power. Her prayers, she said, could not be <mark class="voc">sugar-free</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 塔妮莎·盖克瓦德，已经几乎把糖从自己的饮食里戒掉了。可她还是去糖果店排了队，买了一小盒拉杜——要供在祭台上，献给吉祥天女，一位掌管财富与力量的女神。她说，她的祷告，不能是无糖的。

notes.en: all but means almost completely; very nearly
notes.ctx: 她自己不吃了，但还是要排队去买最甜的那种供神。
notes.ex1: By the time help arrived, the game was all but over. 救援赶到时，比赛差不多已经结束了。
notes.ex2: The old town was all but destroyed by the earthquake. 那座老城几乎被地震彻底毁掉。

notes.en: join the line means to go and stand at the end of a queue of people waiting
notes.zh: 她跟着大家一起排队等
notes.ctx: 戒了糖的人，为了供神又站回了那条队里。
notes.ex1: She joined the line outside the shop and waited her turn. 她在店外排进队伍，等着轮到自己。
notes.ex2: People were joining the line before the shop had even opened. 店还没开门，人们就已经在排队了。

notes.en: altar (n.) means a table or raised surface used for religious ceremonies
notes.ctx: 她买的拉杜不是零食，是摆到台上去的东西。
notes.ex1: She placed the small box of sweets on the altar. 她把那一小盒甜食摆上了供台。
notes.ex2: Flowers are laid at the altar every morning. 每天早上，都有人把鲜花供在祭坛前。

notes.en: sugar-free (adj.) means containing no sugar (the suffix -free means 'without')
notes.ctx: 把食品标签上的词贴到了“祷告”上，这是全文最漂亮的一处双关；她戒了糖，但没戒掉希望。
notes.ex1: She has all but cut sugar from her diet, but her prayers cannot be sugar-free. 她几乎把糖从饮食里戒掉了，可她的祷告不能是无糖的。
notes.ex2: The shop sells a range of sugar-free drinks. 这家店卖一系列无糖饮料。

proper.name: El Niño（厄尔尼诺）
proper.def:
西班牙语，字面意思是“小男孩”，全名 El Niño de Navidad，即“圣诞的圣婴”。十九世纪秘鲁渔民发现每年圣诞节前后沿岸海水异常变暖、鱼群消失、渔获归零，于是管这股暖流叫“圣婴”。它是发生在赤道太平洋的周期性气候现象，会扰乱全球天气：通常给印度、泰国带来高温干旱，给巴西带来多雨寡照。2026 年6 月11 日，美国国家海洋和大气管理局（NOAA）正式宣布厄尔尼诺形成，判断其夏秋季发展为“超强”级别的概率为63%、持续至冬季的概率为96%；中国国家气候中心的判断为“强至超强”东部型。上一次这个量级是1997-98 和2015-16 两次。
本文中的意思：全文标题的第一个词，也是整场危机的总源头。它的名字来历——“带来厄运的圣婴”——与第十段那句“祷告不能无糖”形成一条宗教意象暗线：让甘蔗枯死的叫“圣婴”，而人们在节日里仍然把甜食供到神的面前。

proper.name: Marathwada（马拉特瓦达）
proper.def:
印度马哈拉施特拉邦内的一个地区，也是该邦甘蔗核心产区之一。2026 年9 月25 日，马哈拉施特拉邦宣布全邦358 个taluka（小区）中有265 个——约七成四——被划为旱区，全邦6-9 月降雨亏缺18.8%。
本文中的意思：全文三个农民（帕蒂尔、戈马雷、帕迪尔）和那条干河床所在的地方；它既是甘蔗产区，也是旱情最重的地方——甘蔗把水喝光，水没了又种不成甘蔗，这个死循环就发生在这一片地上。

proper.name: Latur（拉图尔）
proper.def:
马拉特瓦达地区内的一座城市。
本文中的意思：第六段那个21 岁大学生阿迪蒂亚所在的地方。作者刻意让种甘蔗的人和骑摩托车的人住在同一片地上——他们被同一根甘蔗拴在一起。

proper.name: Hero（Hero MotoCorp，英雄摩托）
proper.def:
印度本土摩托车制造商，也是这个国家最大的两轮车生产商之一。印度是全球最大的两轮车市场，全国有两亿多辆摩托车在跑。
本文中的意思：第六段阿迪蒂亚那辆2018 款摩托车的品牌。在印度，摩托车不是玩具，是腿——所以它才是E20 政策落到普通人身上的那个载体。

proper.name: laddoo（拉杜）
proper.def:
印度最常见的传统甜食之一，用豆粉、酥油和糖搓成的小球，圆滚金黄，主要用于过节和供神。
本文中的意思：第十段里那盒被供上祭坛的甜食。它是这篇文章最后那句双关的实物：姑娘自己已经戒糖，却还是排队买下了最甜的它。

proper.name: Mahalaxmi（吉祥天女）
proper.def:
印度教女神，掌管财富、繁荣与力量。十月的印度教节日季（九夜节、十胜节、排灯节）里，她是主要的供奉对象之一。
本文中的意思：第十段供台的主人。姑娘向一位“财富与力量”的女神祷告——而在这个国家，那份用来表达敬意的甜，今年贵得快要供不起了。

proper.name: Manjara River（曼贾拉河）
proper.def:
流经马拉特瓦达地区的一条河流。
本文中的意思：第七段里那座“水坝变成干沟”的河。作者用它把“缺水”这件事，从一口井扩展到整条河。

proper.name: E20（含20% 乙醇的汽油）
proper.def:
印度推行的乙醇混合汽油标准：在汽油中掺入20% 由甘蔗等作物制成的乙醇。2026 年4 月，印度政府把E20 定为全国每一个加油站的标配燃油，并取消了高比例乙醇汽油的生产税。
本文中的意思：第五段那项 government directive 的产物，也是全篇最反常识之处的原点：政府想用甘蔗省油，甘蔗一少糖价就飞，为压糖价又得限制甘蔗去做乙醇——政策的两头在抢同一根甘蔗。

sources_note: 资料核对：以上背景依据文章内容与课件【背景信息/专有名词】整理，并参考美国国家海洋和大气管理局（NOAA）、中国国家气候中心及印度马哈拉施特拉邦政府 2026 年的公开信息。

practice.intro: 请根据今天学习的外刊，把下面的中文句子翻译成英文。要求：尽量用上本文的核心表达，可以适当改变词形，但不要直接照抄原文。
items: 冲突。气候变化。一场正在让万物枯萎的厄尔尼诺。这三样东西像是商量好了似的，一起来毁掉全世界那份嗜甜的快乐。（conspire / spoil / sweet tooth / wither）
全球糖价一路飙升——一个又热又干的夏天，把世界上大片产糖区烤得焦头烂额，顺手把整体食品价格也往上顶了一顶。（soar / scorch / nudge）
而这份痛，没有哪个地方感受得比印度更深切。十一年来最糟糕的一场季风，加上对甘蔗歉收的恐惧，把糖价猛地戳了上去。（acutely / monsoon / spike）
甘蔗正是这个国家生物燃料计划的关键作物——这一点尤其要命，因为印度正想方设法压住石油进口，偏偏中东的航道又被战争掐住了。（biofuels push / curb / choke）
所以，38 岁的戈马雷先生今年把更多的地，押给了甘蔗。适得其反。（devote ... to / backfire）
塔妮莎·盖克瓦德几乎已经把糖从自己的饮食里戒掉了。可她说，她的祷告，不能是无糖的。（all but / cut ... from / sugar-free）
practice.critical_en: When a crop feeds both people and fuel tanks, who should get it first — and who decides?
practice.critical_zh: 当一种作物既要喂饱人、又要喂饱油箱，应该先给谁——又该由谁来决定？
practice.answer:
1. Conflict. Climate change. A withering El Niño. All are conspiring to spoil the world's sweet tooth.

2. Global sugar prices have soared, as a hot, dry summer scorched much of the sugar-producing parts of the world, nudging overall food prices upward.

3. Nowhere is that felt as acutely as it is in India. The worst monsoon in 11 years and fears of a poor sugarcane harvest have spiked prices.

4. Sugarcane is a key crop for the country's biofuels push, all the more so as India seeks to curb oil imports while the waterways of the Middle East are choked by war.

5. So Mr. Gomare, 38, devoted more of his land to sugarcane this year. It backfired.

6. Tanisha Gaikwad had all but cut sugar from her diet. Her prayers, she said, could not be sugar-free.
